candidates.reason: Holds the tests that literally wait on the engine heartbeat: TestMain::test_sleep runs four 2-second sleeps while its MemoryScheduler reports pending requests but returns None, so the crawl only advances when ExecutionEngine._slot.heartbeat fires every _SLOT_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL (5.0s by default). TestRequestSendOrder carries the timing-sensitive `seconds` values (comments 'increase if flaky') that also depend on engine nextcall scheduling. Any change that speeds up heartbeat-driven waits must update this module.

Directly asserts the heartbeat lifecycle on the engine slot: test_exception_slot deletes engine._slot.heartbeat to trigger the 'Slot close failure' path, and the other tests exercise ExecutionEngine.close_spider_async/_Slot._maybe_fire_closing, which is exactly the code that cancels nextcall and stops the heartbeat. Relevant if the heartbeat stops being started/stopped unconditionally.

End-to-end ExecutionEngine tests (built on tests/utils/engine.py CrawlerRun + TestEngineBase): they drive open_spider_async/close, spider_idle/close handling and the start-request processing loop where ExecutionEngine._start_request_processing starts the heartbeat, so a heartbeat change is observable here.

Already works around the engine heartbeat by monkeypatching engine_mod.create_looping_call with OneShotLoop/TwoShotLoop to avoid a background LoopingCall and engine start/stop races. If the heartbeat scheduling or its test stubbing changes, these tests must be adapted; they are the existing precedent for neutralizing the heartbeat in tests.

Unit tests for the scheduling primitive the engine heartbeat is built on (scrapy.utils.asyncio.create_looping_call/AsyncioLoopingCall, used as _Slot.heartbeat). Start/stop/now/interval semantics asserted here are what the heartbeat relies on, so they are the closest lower-level candidate if the heartbeat's interval or loop handling is modified.
